_readme: Keyword queue for the Schiano Studios blog. Cron drafts the first entry whose slug is not already in the CMS (draft, live or archived). Volumes and KD are SEMrush US, pulled 2026-10-08 (first 12 via Keyword Magic, rest via the SEMrush API, KD under 30). Add new rows at the bottom; never reuse a slug.

queue.angle: Help a small business owner choose between Webflow and WordPress based on who will edit the site, how much plugin upkeep they can handle, design flexibility, and hosting. No prices.
What a contractor website needs so homeowners call: service area, licensing and insurance info, project photos, a simple quote form, and click to call on mobile.
Compare Framer and Webflow for a small business site: CMS needs, who maintains it, SEO controls, and when each one fits. No prices or feature lists that change often.
Design decisions for a general contractor site: page structure by service, project gallery that loads fast, trust details, and a quote request flow.
When a small business outgrows Squarespace and when it does not. Focus on CMS structure, design control, and who edits the site.
Wix versus Webflow for a local business: ease of editing, design limits, SEO settings, and moving later.
What a restaurant site needs on a phone: menu as real text not a PDF, hours, location, reservations or ordering link, and photos that load fast.
Local SEO basics for a roofing contractor site: service area pages, Google Business Profile, page titles, project photos with alt text, and reviews.
A checklist to evaluate an HVAC contractor website: emergency contact visibility, service pages, financing info placement, mobile speed, and booking.
Webflow versus Shopify for a small brand that sells online: catalog size, checkout needs, content and design, and when to combine them.
The five pages every contractor site should have and what goes on each one.
Webflow builds marketing websites, Bubble builds web apps. Explain the difference and how a business decides which it needs.
Explain what Webflow is to a business owner: visual builder, CMS, hosting, who it suits and who it does not. No prices or plan details.
What a plumber's website needs: emergency call button, service area, services list, license info, reviews, and fast mobile pages.
When Webflow is not the right fit and what kinds of tools fit instead (WordPress, Squarespace, Shopify, Framer), framed by business needs. No prices.

What a therapy practice site needs: calm design, clear specialties, insurance and fees page placeholder guidance, booking, privacy. Note that privacy rules should be confirmed with their own compliance advisor; give no legal advice.
A monthly and quarterly maintenance checklist for a small business site: content, forms, links, backups, speed, security updates, analytics.
What a dental practice site needs: services pages, new patient info, booking, insurance info placement, location and hours, mobile speed.
How to hire a Webflow designer: what to ask, how to review a portfolio, what a good process looks like, and red flags. No prices.
The traits strong contractor websites share. Do not name or describe real companies; describe patterns and give hypothetical examples.
What a medical practice site needs: provider bios, services, patient forms, booking, accessibility. Privacy rules should be confirmed with their compliance advisor; no legal advice.
Describe hypothetical example layouts for different small business types (restaurant, contractor, salon, practice) and why each structure works. Do not name real businesses.
What a roofing company site needs: storm and emergency messaging, service area, project galleries, financing info placement, quote form.
When Webflow ecommerce fits a small shop and when a dedicated store platform fits better, based on catalog size and checkout needs. No prices or plan limits.
Who should own what on a small business website: content updates, technical upkeep, domains and logins, and how to decide between doing it in house or hiring help.
What a manufacturer's site needs: capabilities pages, industries served, certifications, RFQ form, spec sheets, and a structure buyers can scan.
What a painting contractor site needs: before and after galleries that load fast, residential vs commercial pages, estimate form, service area.
What a home builder site needs: communities or project portfolio, process page, floor plans presentation, inquiry flow.
How to measure a Webflow site: options for analytics, connecting Google Analytics 4 and Tag Manager, tracking form submissions. Avoid plan specific feature claims.
What a small business website package should include and questions to ask before buying one: pages, CMS, hosting, ownership of domain and content, support. No prices.
What a construction company site needs for commercial clients: capabilities, project case pages structure, safety and certifications, bid request flow.
What an electrical contractor site needs: residential vs commercial services, emergency contact, licensing info, quote form, local pages.
What a financial advisor site needs: clear services, who they serve, team bios, booking. Compliance review of site copy should go through their firm; no legal or financial advice.
What a school website needs: parent focused navigation, calendar and announcements, admissions path, accessibility, and easy staff editing.
What a family law firm site needs: practice area pages, attorney bios, a calm tone, consultation booking. No legal advice; attorney advertising rules should be confirmed by the firm.

servicePageTargets._note: Hiring intent keywords. These need real service pages, not blog posts. Do not draft these as articles.
